title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 332 (Effect of floating charge)

content.overview: Where a company is being wound up, a floating charge on the undertaking or property of the company created within the twelve months immediately preceding the commencement of the winding up is invalid, unless it is proved that the company was solvent immediately after the creation of the charge, except for the amount of any cash paid to the company at the time of or subsequent to the creation of, and in consideration for, the charge, together with interest at five per cent.
content.glance: Floating charges created within twelve months before winding up are invalid unless the company was then solvent; exception for new cash consideration plus 5% interest.
content.study: Section 332 restricts the effectiveness of late floating charges. A floating charge created within twelve months before commencement of winding up is invalid except to the extent of cash actually paid to the company at or after creation and in consideration for the charge, plus interest at five per cent. The invalidity can be avoided if it is proved that the company was solvent immediately after the charge was created. The provision protects the estate against last-minute floating security that does not inject fresh value.

sections.heading: Invalidity of late floating charge
sections.body: Floating charge created within twelve months before commencement of winding up is invalid unless company proved solvent immediately after creation.

sections.heading: Cash exception
sections.body: Valid to the extent of cash paid at or after creation in consideration for the charge, plus interest at five per cent.

examples.title: Late floating charge without new cash
examples.body: Nine months before winding up the company grants a floating charge over all assets to secure pre-existing debt without any fresh cash advance. Unless solvency immediately after creation is proved, the charge is invalid under s. 332.

examples.title: Fresh cash exception
examples.body: A floating charge is granted within the twelve-month window in exchange for a contemporaneous cash loan of ₹50 lakh. The charge remains valid to the extent of that cash plus five per cent interest.

hypotheticals.question: Is a floating charge created ten months before winding up automatically void?
hypotheticals.analysis: It is invalid unless the company is proved to have been solvent immediately after creation, or to the extent of any cash paid in consideration plus 5% interest.

distinctions.title: s. 332 vs preferential priority over floating charge

rows.left: Validity of the floating charge itself
rows.right: Priority of preferential debts over floating-charge claims when general assets insufficient

misconceptions.trap: Every floating charge created within twelve months is completely void.
misconceptions.correction: It is invalid unless solvency is proved, and remains valid to the extent of new cash consideration plus 5% interest.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 332 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm floating charge and twelve-month window. II. Test solvency immediately after creation. III. Quantify any cash consideration and apply the 5% interest exception.

examTips: State the twelve-month rule, the solvency escape, and the cash-plus-5% exception.
revisionPoints: Late floating charges invalid unless solvent or new cash
